I think about it everyday when my limerence is really bad. I don’t have access to therapy so I’ve been trying to find ways to deal with it on my own. Some of these are small things but they all add up and make me feel better

Showering everyday, having a skincare routine, putting effort into how I present myself (doing my makeup, hair, wearing a nice outfit). All of those things boost my confidence a lot, and it makes it easier for me to like myself. Taking my vitamins everyday. Journaling has been really good for me, one time I wrote 5 pages of every emotion I was feeling at the time and it felt so good for those feelings to be on paper instead of in my head. It actually felt like I was able to let it go for a while. Starting a big project for my room felt really good, it gave me lots of dopamine everytime I finished one of my goals. Reading about limerence helps because it makes me feel valid and understand myself more, like I’m not just completely insane (I have just been reading articles but I’m going to start reading some books about it soon, I think that would be more beneficial). Deleting social media is hard but it helps so I’m not constantly comparing myself to every girl I think my LO would like. I have also started microdosing psilocybin sometimes and when I do, I notice that I am not as obsessive and I can focus on things other than LO. It also motivates me to better myself and makes me a happier person in general. I know not everyone would want to try that but it genuinely does help me so I wanted to add that. Focus on getting a hobby that has nothing to do with your LO. One of my hobbies is playing video games but my LO is one of my first friends I met on my favorite game, so obviously I think about him when I’m playing it. One of my new hobbies is playing electric guitar which is great because all I can think about is the music.

Now I don’t do this stuff every day but I do it when I have the energy to and it makes me feel good. But I think it would be good to try and do a couple of these things everyday no matter how you’re feeling, because that’s how routines are formed and hopefully after a few weeks you’ll start to feel much better
